llm.summary: This is a documentation-only hook-authoring skill with purpose-aligned examples, but users should review logging, network, and persistence examples before copying them.

dimensions.detail: The guide discusses global hooks, HTTP hooks, local project-file reads, and audit logs; these are coherent for hook authoring but can affect all sessions or expose data if copied without review.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The artifact contains markdown guidance only; no executable files, install scripts, bundled hooks, or automatic runtime activation were present.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Most sensitive examples are disclosed as hook examples, but a few broad audit/context-injection snippets should be narrowed or sanitized before use in real projects.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Persistent logs and state files under ~/.claude are shown as examples and are not installed automatically; users should add retention, permissions, and redaction if implementing them.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The skill consistently presents itself as guidance for Claude Code and Claude Agent SDK hook authoring, including validation, logging, context injection, performance, and testing patterns.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Installers can treat this as a hook-authoring reference, not an active hook package. Before copying examples, avoid logging raw tool input or output, review any HTTP hook destinations, make project-file context injection explicit, and add file permissions, retention, and redaction for local logs or state.
llm.findings:
[SQP-2] expected: The copy-paste cleanup command example is part of observability-hook guidance and is explicitly scoped to binary-actionable cleanup, but users should treat rm -rf examples as destructive and review paths first.
[SQP-2] expected: Async file and HTTP examples are expected in a performance guide for hooks; they are examples rather than active code, though production versions should minimize, redact, and allowlist data flows.
[SQP-2] expected: Audit-log batching examples store operational metadata, which fits the logging purpose, but deployed hooks should define retention and avoid sensitive payloads.
[SQP-2] unexpected: The raw $CLAUDE_TOOL_INPUT global audit-log example is broader than necessary for a security-first guide and should be sanitized before use, but it is visible example code rather than hidden behavior.
[SQP-2] expected: The context-injection example reads README, conventions, and architecture files for prompt enrichment, which matches the skill purpose; users should make this opt-in for confidential projects.
[RA2] expected: The persistent state example stores only counters in a local file and is disclosed as cross-session state, so it is proportionate as a sample but should use restrictive permissions in production.
[RA2] expected: Cross-session state is a normal hook pattern in this guide and is not automatically enabled by the skill; the risk is mainly copy-and-paste use without lifecycle controls.
